quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane to see other vehicles better.
Ride close behind the vehicle in front of you to use their headlights.
Slow down to help you avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to help you avoid unexpected hazards.
questions.explanation: At night, ride slower than you would during the day. This gives you a better chance to avoid hazards. Also increase your following distance and be flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Most conflicts between motorcycles and other vehicles happen at intersections.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns you that the signal will soon turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: How should you position your body on the motorcycle?

options.text: Hold yourself up with your arms.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your elbows should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It brakes automatically by learning your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving while riding over bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross the surface faster.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on bridge gratings, keep a steady speed and go straight across. Zigzagging to stay in your lane is dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel below 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn carts.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed in a group?

options.text: At the front leading the group
Near the front of the group
At the back of the group

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the front of the group
questions.explanation: Place less experienced riders near the front behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can lead and watch the newer riders at the same time.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space and proceed with caution. Always slow down and be ready to stop at an emergency scene.

questions.question: What can cause motorcycle collisions?

options.text: Following too closely behind another vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Following too closely behind another vehicle
questions.explanation: Following too closely, called tailgating, can cause motorcycle collisions. Always keep a safe distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: How can other drivers see you more easily?
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing to help other drivers see you. This works during the day and at night.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle and car accidents happen?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle and car accidents happen at intersections. Usually, the car driver fails to give the motorcycle driver the right-of-way.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is not as loud as a car's horn. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it to keep you safe.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left portion of your lane.
The center portion of your lane.
The right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle is dangerous. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to return to your lane too quickly.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power does the front brake provide?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing to be more visible when riding, even during the day. Reflective clothing also helps.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Your mirrors can show you everything around you.
Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for blind spots.
Use your turn signal and move right or left immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always check your mirrors and turn your head to see your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect your riding ability?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride safely. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle is more powerful?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What is Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) designed to do?

options.text: Stop the wheels from locking up and skidding.
Lock up the wheels while keeping control.
Keep riders from braking on wet roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from locking up and skidding.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents your wheels from locking and skidding when you brake hard. It works by releasing and re-applying brake pressure many times per second. This keeps your wheels turning so you can stop safely and stay in control.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to finish the pass.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.explanation: You must complete all passes within the posted speed limit. Only pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should your feet be?
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests at all times. Do not point your toes down, as they can get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: In normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead in normal conditions. Use more distance if road or weather conditions are poor.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert you to road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.
